en.title: Fresh snow in Courchevel next week: up to 42 cm on the upper slopes (23–29 November 2026)
en.description: Courchevel gets 27 cm at the top 23–29 November, with Wednesday 25 as the heaviest day. Forecast from 16 November.
en.lede: Courchevel's upper slopes gain 27 cm between 23 and 29 November, stacked onto 85 cm that falls this week. Wednesday 25 November brings the peak: 8 cm (range up to 8 cm) on the highest terrain.

sections.h: This week's heavy fall sets up next week
p: Before the November 23–29 snow arrives, Courchevel is busy this week. The top gains 85 cm between 17 and 20 November (ranging from 63 to 106 cm), while the base stays almost dry at 5 cm. That deep upper layer matters: next week's fresh snow will land on a foundation, not bare rock.
The base level today sits at only 5 cm. Next week's 17 cm there will be half what falls higher up, so elevation becomes the key to good turns.

sections.h: Where the snow falls by altitude
p: Drop down the mountain and the numbers shrink steadily. Near 2500 m (the top lift area), expect 27 cm. Around 2000 m (mid-mountain), it falls to 26 cm. At 1300 m (the base), only 17 cm accumulates. The uncertainty widens at height: the top could see as little as 12 cm or as much as 42 cm, while the base's range is tighter at 4 to 30 cm.

Three days pack most of the snow. Wednesday 25 November brings 8 cm to the top (up to 8 cm in the high case). Thursday 26 adds another 8 cm (up to 12 cm). Sunday 29 contributes 6 cm (up to 10 cm). All other days in that week yield barely a dusting.

sections.h: The best terrain for fresh snow
p: Saulire and the high bowls above Courchevel 1850 will hold the deepest, cleanest snow. The north-facing Courchevel side and the tree-lined slopes above Le Praz reward you most when light goes flat. In poor visibility, those trees break the sky and guide your line.

Lower runs at Le Praz and La Tania, tucked in the forest, will turn sluggish first if mild air moves in mid-week. The base stays thin relative to the top, so early-season rocks are a real risk on the lower forest runs.

If you can choose when to ski, pick the day after Wednesday 25 November. By then, Wednesday's fresh snow (8 cm, up to 8 cm) has settled just enough to track smoothly into the trees without feeling tracked out. You miss the peak-day crowds and ride the gift it leaves behind.
Courchevel's famous grooming means fresh snow gets pisted fast. Early lifts are your friend; late starts mean harder snow.

A forecast seven to thirteen days out shows a trend, not a fixed plan. The timing is more reliable than the total: Wednesday 25 is likely the heaviest day, but the amount could swing from 12 cm to 42 cm. The range is wide because the Forecasts disagree on storm intensity.

Among your neighbours, Val Thorens (14 km away) tops the week with 30 cm at its top; La Plagne and Méribel (both near Courchevel) match at 28 cm each. Courchevel's 27 cm puts it in the same league. Terrain and grooming, not just snow depth, pick the winner.

sections.h: What to pack and watch for
p: Early season means thin coverage. Even 17 cm at the base is not thick enough to hide all hazards; rocks can punch through. Stay on marked runs or check official hazard reports if you venture off.

Off the groomed slopes, new snow creates new avalanche risk. The French avalanche bulletin (BERA) for the massif is your safety source. Plan your day around the top's 27 cm, and treat anything above that as a bonus.

advice: Wednesday 25 November is the peak snow day; plan to be on the upper slopes (Saulire, the high bowls, north-facing Courchevel side) when the heaviest falls arrive.
Ski Thursday 26 or later if you want fresh snow that has settled enough to track smoothly but is not yet skied out.
Avoid the lower runs (Le Praz, La Tania, the base) in the first days after snow if the forecast turns mild; heavy, sticky snow sets in fast at low altitude.
Early lifts matter: Courchevel's grooming clears fresh snow quickly, so late starts mean harder, faster snow.
Off-piste: new snow means new avalanche risk. Check the BERA before you leave the groomed runs.
